task_reconstruction.official_task: 2023 MCM Problem C, Wordle reporting, addressed to the New York Times puzzle editor.
required_outputs: a distribution of attempts for a given word
a forecast of reported results on a future date
the share of those reports that are hard mode
a letter to the puzzle editor

section_map.summary: abstract: three questions, subset entropy, three submodels, one causal claim
introduction: rules, tiles, the WordleStats bot
data: seven repaired cells, percentages turned back into counts
model-establishment: positional entropy and subset entropy
model-establishment: beta summary of the seven shares
results: causation under random word choice, then a null weekday effect
memo: letter to the puzzle editor

contributions.summary: Subset entropy is the expected log shrink of the candidate pool after one guess.
Two beta parameters stand in for the seven attempt shares.
Conditional independence splits one large posterior into three sampler runs.
A causal reading is tied to the assumption that the words are chosen at random.

dependency_graph.label: Four traits score the attempt split.
The report count is the multinomial total.
The report count is the binomial total.

assumptions.summary: Words with more vowels are easier, and y is not a vowel.
Players open with one of thirty high-overlap words.
Normal(0, 20) is wide enough to be uninformative.
The Times choose the word at random.
Player skill does not change across days.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Seven repaired cells, each logged: hard-mode counts, tash, clen, naive, rprobe, and the 2569 to 25569 report count.
Rounded percentages are rescaled by their row sum, then restored to integers by largest remainder.
Stanford GraphBase list of 5757 five-letter words.

models.summary: MU-C-Q242-001: positional entropy, subset entropy, beta summary.

verification.summary: Retrodiction tracks the long trend of reports and of hard-mode share.
Fungi: posterior bars against the observed shares.
Eerie: difficulty ratio about 0.52, near the 50th percentile of past words.

results_trace.summary: Four surviving traits: unique letters, usage, average yellow tiles, subset entropy.
Reports for eerie on 1 March 2023: [20238, 27876], median 23884.
Hard-mode share: [9.97, 12.62], median 11.25. Hard-mode count median 2683.
Fourth-guess share median 22.46. The failure row in the printed table is shifted.

writing_logic.summary: The summary asks three questions before it names a model.
A feature is motivated, then defined, then read.
Cause is flagged as intentional, then earned by the random-choice assumption.
The letter leads with the finding and leaves the sampler for the signature.

language_observations.summary: Three very natural questions arise. Not just, but full posterior distributions.
A reasonable question to ask is how much. It seems justified to consider.
Beyond just Poisson error, we must. Rather than simple point estimates.
The word cause is used intentionally. Surprisingly, centered around zero.
We discovered that. We are sure you will agree. Happy Puzzling.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The causal claim is only as strong as the random-choice assumption, which the paper states.
The letter answers the editor who picks the word, in that editor's terms.

weaknesses.summary: The printed multinomial probability vector omits one entry.
Table 1 shifts the one-guess interval onto the two-guess row.
No autocorrelation, so the long-horizon bands may be too narrow.

independent_extensions.summary: Add a second-guess entropy for the atch case the paper names and leaves out.
Put an autoregressive term on the report-count residual and widen the March interval.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Number the questions before naming the model.
Put the assumption in the same sentence as the causal verb.
